summary_en: Why do some regions bounce back from shocks while others do not? Elekes maps inter-industry labour flows across 72 Swedish local labour markets and asks which network features predict resilience to negative shocks. He finds that regions with more diverse, skill-related cross-industry flows recover faster: the network of where workers can plausibly move when their sector falters is itself an economic asset, separate from the region's industrial mix.
data_used: Swedish administrative microdata (LISA-type registers) on annual worker–establishment matches, used to construct inter-industry labour-flow networks at the local-labour-market level for 72 Swedish regions. Resilience proxies built from regional employment trajectories around shocks.
policy_relevance: Useful frame for Hungarian county-level economic-development plans and EFRE programming: resilience to plant closures, sectoral shocks, or trade reversals depends on how easily local workers can rotate across related industries. For Hungary's mono-industry regions (e.g., automotive clusters in Győr / Kecskemét, agro-processing in Békés), the policy lever isn't only sectoral subsidies but active fostering of skill-adjacent industries that workers could plausibly move into.
title: Regional resilience and the network structure of inter-industry labour flows
